newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI SAGS, BUT AAMULEHTI SOARS ON MERGER PLAN.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI SAGS, BUT AAMULEHTI SOARS ON MERGER PLAN.

text.p: Shares sagged in thin trade on
Tuesday and were seen remaining soft with nothing in view to
turn the day's trend, while Aamulehti grabbed the spotlight with
a merger that sent its stock soaring, brokers said.
Aamulehti surged to record highs after announcing plans to
merge with Finnish commercial television group MTV Oy that would
make it Finland's biggest media group.
Aamulehti traded up 35.00 markka at 190.00, after hitting an
all-time high 195.00 in fair 6.5 million markka trade on an
otherwise quiet bourse.
Nokia hovered slightly above its lower Wall Street close.
The telecoms share fell 1.50 markka to 301.50, but came off
a session low of 299.00 in thin 27 million markka tunrover.
Forestries were soft, with UPM-Kymmene down 1.50 to 113.00
and off 0.70 at 41.50.
Orion went ex-dividend and fell 5.00 markka, matching the
amount of its dividend, in lively 25 million markka trade.
Brokers said volume could easily remain thin this week in
the absence of market-moving indicators, but that next week
trade would be boosted by Nokia's first-quarter report on
Tuesday.
